title: Fudgy Chocolate Layer Cake
description: Chocolate fans will surely applaud this to-die-for fudge cake.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line bottoms of two 9-inch round cake pans with waxed paper. Grease paper and sides of pans. Dust with flour.

Mix flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt. In another bowl, beat butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. Add vanilla.
At low speed, alternately beat flour mixture and buttermilk into butter mixture just until blended. Divide batter equally between prepared pans.
Bake cakes until a toothpick inserted in center comes clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Let cool for 10 minutes. Turn out onto racks. Remove paper. Turn layers top side up and cool completely.
To prepare frosting, beat butter and confectioners' sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add melted chocolate and vanilla; continue beating until shiny and smooth.

Place 1 cake layer on a serving plate; spread with frosting. Top with remaining cake layer. Spread frosting on top and sides of cake. Let cake stand for at least 30 minutes before sprinkling with chocolate shavings.

title: Apple-Oatmeal Cookies
description: These soft, chewy cookies are perfect for filling the cookie jar.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, combine oats, all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon. Stir to combine.
Stir in raisins and apples.
In a large bowl, combine egg, honey, oil and milk. Stir in dry ingredients. Mix to form a smooth batter.
Drop batter onto ungreased baking sheets, using a rounded teaspoon of dough for each cookie, leaving 2 inches between. Dip fingers into water. Press dough down to about 1½ inch diameter.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until lightly golden.
Remove sheet from oven. Transfer cookies to cooling rack.

notes: Check cookies while baking to make sure they are not getting overdone on the bottoms, especially if using a dark colored baking sheet. Dark cookie sheets absorb more heat and tend to burn cookies before baking is complete.

title: Almond Streusel Cake
source_note: Great American Home Baking, 8 Coffee Cakes, Card 3
description: Transform a plain cake into an irresistible delight with a crumbly almond streusel.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9- or 10-inch tube pan.
To prepare the streusel, in a medium bowl, mix together brown sugar, nuts, and flour. Stir in the butter and zest.

To prepare cake, in a large bowl, using an electric mixer set on medium speed, beat together butter and sugar until fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in zest and vanilla.
In a large bowl, mix together the flour, baking powder, and baking soda.
Reduce mixer speed to low. Alternately beat flour mixture and orange juice into egg mixture, beginning and ending with flour.
Spoon half of the batter into prepared pan. Sprinkle with half of the streusel. Top with the remaining batter and streusel.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack to cool completely.
To prepare the glaze, in a cup, stir together confectioners' sugar and orange juice until smooth.
Turn the cake out onto a serving plate, placing it right-side up. Drizzle with the glaze.

notes: For a different streusel mixture, substitute chopped walnuts for the almonds.

title: Bacon and Double Cheese Quiche
description: Paired with a tossed green salad, this full-flavored quiche makes an excellent lunch.

ingredients.item: chilled butter, cut into small pieces

instructions.text: To prepare the crust, in a large bowl, mix together the flour and salt. Using a pastry blender or 2 knives, cut in the butter until coarse crumbs form.
Add water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with a fork, until a dough forms. Shape into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill in refrigerator for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). On a lightly floured surface, using a lightly floured rolling pin, roll the dough into 11-inch circle. Fit into 9-inch pie pan. Trim edge, leaving ½-inch overhang. Fold under to form standup edge. Prick dough with a fork. Line with foil and fill with pie weights or dried beans.
Bake for 10 minutes. Remove the foil and weights. Bake until lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.
Meanwhile, prepare filling. In a medium skillet, cook the bacon over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel to drain.

In a small bowl, whisk together the eggs, cream, thyme, and pepper. Pour into crust. Crumble bacon. Sprinkle the egg mixture with the bacon, Gruyère cheese, and Cheddar cheese. Bake until golden and custard is set, about 30 minutes. Serve warm.

notes: To freeze: Cool baked quiche completely, wrap airtight, and freeze for up to 1 month.

Shape into 1-inch balls. Place 1 1/2 inch apart on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 325 degrees until tinged with brown, cool some. Then roll in powdered sugar. Enjoy.

Melt butter and marshmallows in saucepan. Add vanilla, food coloring, and corn flakes.

title: Sandwich Loaf
description: Ideal for luncheons, parties & holidays. These may be made longer to feed more by using more slices of bread & filling.

ingredients.item: tuna fish, pimento cheese, & egg salad fillings

instructions.text: Loaf turns out more colorful by using greens of different colors. Prepare 3 salads, such as tuna fish, pimento cheese, & egg salad (or others that you prefer).

Cut edges off of 1/2 slices of thin sliced white bread. Lay 3 slices down flat in a straight line & spread with tuna. Lay 3 more bread slices on top of tuna and spread pimento cheese. Lay 3 more bread slices on top of cheese. Make sure bread is stacked neatly and closely. Spread with egg salad. Try 3 more slices on top of egg salad.

title: Ham & Cream Cheese Roll Ups

ingredients.item: pkgs of medium sliced Honey Ham Lunch Meat (not the fat free!)
jar of black small pitted olives

instructions.text: Lay one slice of ham on cutting board, spread a layer of cream cheese on ham, roll then slice into small pieces.
Use toothpicks to hold olives on top and to hold roll together.

notes: Amount depends on number desired to make

title: Fudgy Chocolate Layer Cake
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 5 - Cakes

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line bottoms of two 9-inch round cake pans with waxed paper. Grease paper and sides of pans. Dust with flour.

Mix flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt. In another bowl, beat butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. Add vanilla.
At low speed, alternately beat flour mixture and buttermilk into butter mixture, just until blended. Divide batter equally between prepared pans.
Bake cakes until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Turn out onto racks. Remove paper. Turn layers top side up and cool completely.
To prepare frosting, beat butter and confectioners' sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add melted chocolate and vanilla; continue beating until shiny and smooth.
Place 1 cake layer on a serving plate; spread with frosting. Top with remaining cake layer. Spread frosting on top and sides of cake.

title: Apple-Oatmeal Cookies
description: These soft, chewy cookies are perfect for filling the cookie jar.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a medium bowl, combine oats, flours, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
Stir in raisins and apples.
In a large bowl, combine egg, honey, oil and milk. Stir in dry ingredients. Mix to form a smooth batter.
Drop batter onto ungreased baking sheets, using a rounded teaspoon of dough for each cookie, leaving 2 inches between.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until lightly golden.
Transfer cookies to cooling rack.

title: Almond Streusel Cake
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 3 - Coffee Cakes
description: Transform a plain cake into an irresistible delight with a crumbly almond streusel.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9- or 10-inch tube pan.
To prepare streusel, mix together brown sugar, nuts, and flour. Stir in the butter.
To prepare cake, beat butter and sugar until fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well.
Mix flour, baking powder, and baking soda. Alternately beat flour mixture and orange juice into egg mixture.
Spoon half of batter into pan. Sprinkle with half of streusel. Top with remaining batter and streusel.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes. Cool completely.
For glaze, stir confectioners' sugar and orange juice until smooth. Drizzle over cake.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 2 - Main Dish Baking
description: Using leftover cooked chicken cuts the preparation time in this flavorful pot pie.

instructions.text: To prepare pastry, mix flour and salt. Cut butter into flour until coarse crumbs form.
Whisk egg and ice water. Shape into disk, wrap, chill 1 hour.
Place chicken in 2-quart casserole.
Melt butter, sauté mushrooms until browned. Add wine, cook 2 minutes. Add to chicken.
Whisk cream, flour, paprika over low heat. Add to chicken mixture.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Roll pastry to fit top of pie. Trim and seal edges.
Brush with egg glaze. Cut decorations from trimmings.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until bubbly and browned. Serve warm.

title: Fresh Berry Crumb Pie
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 2 - Cobblers, Custards & Fruit Crisps
description: A hazelnut mixture does double duty as a crust and topping in this berry-filled pie.

ingredients.item: chilled butter, cut into pieces (crumb crust/topping)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F. To prepare crumb crust/topping, spread nuts in a medium baking pan. Roast the nuts, stirring occasionally, until toasted, about 10 minutes.
Remove nuts from the oven and turn out onto a cloth towel. Rub off and discard the papery skins. Increase the oven temperature to 450°F.
In a food processor fitted with the metal blade, process nuts until finely ground, about 10 seconds.
In a large bowl, mix together the nuts, flour, and sugar. Using a pastry blender or 2 knives, cut the butter into the flour mixture until coarse crumbs form.
Using fingers, evenly press half of the crumb crust/topping mixture into the bottom and sides of an 8- or 9-inch tart pan.
To prepare the filling, in a medium bowl, mix together the sugar and the cornstarch. Gently fold in the berries. Spoon the berry mixture into the crust, spreading evenly.
Sprinkle the berry mixture evenly with the remaining crumb crust/topping.
Bake until topping is golden and filling is bubbly, 30 minutes. Transfer the pan to a wire rack to cool for 10 minutes. Serve warm.

notes: Watch nuts very carefully when you are grinding them in the food processor. If you grind them too long, the result will be nut butter.

title: Peach-Apricot Cobbler
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 2 - Cobblers, Custards & Fruit Crisps
description: These two fruits combine beautifully to make a homey, warm-from-the-oven dessert.

ingredients.item: canned sliced peaches, drained, juice reserved
canned apricot halves, drained, juice reserved

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.

In a medium saucepan, mix together sugar and cornstarch. Stir in 1/2 cup each of reserved peach and apricot juices. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture boils and thickens, 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in butter, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Add peaches and apricots. Spoon fruit mixture into a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
To prepare topping, mix together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, butter, and egg. Spoon topping over fruit mixture.
Bake cobbler until topping is lightly golden, 30 minutes. Transfer casserole to a wire rack to cool slightly.
To prepare garnish, beat together cream, honey, and cinnamon at medium speed until soft peaks form.
Serve cobbler warm, topped with spiced whipped cream.

notes: Try this dish with other canned fruit already on your pantry shelf. Use any combination of plums, pears, pineapple, or mandarin oranges.

title: Lemon Meringue Pie
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 13 - Pies & Tarts
description: Sweet meringue offsets the tart citrus flavor in this classic lemon-filled pie.

ingredients.item: 9-inch packaged pie crust, pre-baked if required

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F. To prepare filling, in top of a double boiler, whisk together eggs, egg yolks, sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch. Place over simmering water. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Do not let mixture boil. Remove from over water. Stir in butter. Pour into crust.
To prepare meringue, beat egg whites appear foamy. Beat in cream of tartar until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in sugar and vanilla at high speed until stiff, but not dry, peaks form.
Spoon meringue into a large pastry bag fitted with a star tip. Pipe meringue decoratively over filling to edge of crust. Bake pie until meringue is golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

notes: Make sure the meringue is piped right to the edge of the crust, to prevent the filling from seeping out. When making meringue, it is important not to overbeat the mixture. Adding a pinch of cream of tartar makes the egg whites less prone to overbeating.

title: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Icing
description: A nut-sprinkled cream cheese icing is the perfect foil for this moist, not-too-sweet carrot cake.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-inch round cake pan. Dust with flour; tap out excess.
Mix together flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.

Beat together butter and sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. At low speed, alternately beat flour mixture and milk into butter mixture. Stir in carrots and nuts. Pour batter into prepared pan.

Bake cake until top springs back when lightly touched and a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, 40 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack to cool for 10 minutes. Turn cake out onto rack to cool completely.

To prepare icing, beat together butter and cream cheese at medium speed until completely smooth. Beat in vanilla. Beat in confectioners' sugar until well blended. To prepare topping, mix together nuts and brown sugar.
Place cake on a serving plate. Spread icing over top and sides. Sprinkle with nut mixture.

notes: If desired, icing can be omitted. Instead, dust top of cake with confectioners' sugar.

title: Healthy Apple-Walnut Muffins
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 6 - Quick Breads & Muffins
description: Made with no added fat or sugar, these tasty muffins use fruit and buttermilk to keep them moist.

ingredients.item: small Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and chopped
small Granny Smith apple, for garnish

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease 12 standard size muffin-pan cups or line with paper liners.
Mix together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, allspice, nutmeg, and salt.
Mix together eggs, apple juice, and buttermilk.
Stir flour mixture and oat bran into egg mixture until dry ingredients are just moistened. Do not overmix. Gently stir in chopped apples and nuts.
Spoon batter into prepared pan, filling cups two-thirds full.
Garnish each muffin with an apple slice. Peel, core, and cut garnish apple into 12 thin slices.
Bake muffins until lightly golden and tops spring back when pressed, 25 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. Turn muffins out onto rack to cool completely.

notes: Instead of frozen apple juice concentrate, use other bottled fruit juice concentrates. Health food stores generally carry the best variety. Experiment with such interesting flavors as papaya, pineapple, and mango for a tropical taste.

title: Butter Crescents
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 4 - Biscuits & Rolls
description: Start the day on a high note with a cup of tea and these melt-in-your-mouth crescents.

instructions.text: In a saucepan, heat milk until bubbles appear around edges of pan. Combine butter, sugar, and salt. Add hot milk; stir well. Cool to lukewarm (95-100°F).
In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water. Let stand until foamy, 5 to 10 minutes.

Beat yeast mixture and egg into milk mixture at low speed. Beat in 2 cups of flour at low speed until smooth. Continue beating until thick. Mix in enough remaining flour until dough pulls away from sides of bowl.

On a floured surface, knead dough very gently until smooth and elastic, 2 to 3 minutes. Place in a large greased bowl, turning to coat. Cover loosely with a damp cloth; let rise in a warm place until doubled, 1 hour.
Punch down dough. On a floured surface, divide dough in half. Cover with a damp cloth; let rest for 10 minutes.

Grease 2 baking sheets. Using a floured rolling pin, roll 1 dough half into a 12-inch circle. Cut circle into 6 wedges. Starting at side opposite point, roll up each wedge. Place, point-sides down, on prepared baking sheets. Curve ends to form crescents. Repeat with remaining dough half.
Cover loosely with a damp cloth; let rise in a warm place until almost doubled, 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Brush crescents with glaze. Bake until golden, 15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

notes: Knead dough very gently to keep rolls tender.

title: Chocolate-Pecan Brownies
source_note: Great American Home Baking magazine, Card 13 - Cookies & Candies
description: Ready in less than an hour, these fudgy treats are delightfully sweet and rich.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease a 9-inch square baking pan.
In a small bowl, mix together flour and baking soda.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar, butter, and water. Bring to a boil over medium heat; remove immediately from heat.
Stir in 1 cup of chocolate morsels and vanilla extract until chocolate is melted and mixture is smooth.
Transfer mixture to a medium bowl. Cool completely.
Stir in eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition. Gradually stir in flour mixture until smooth.
Stir remaining chocolate morsels and nuts into batter. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack to cool completely. Cut into squares.

notes: For light, moist brownies, cool chocolate mixture completely before combining it with other ingredients; test for doneness 2 to 3 minutes before the suggested baking time.

title: Baked Meatballs
description: Tender baked meatballs made with a panade for extra moisture.

instructions.text: Make the panade. In a large mixing bowl, stir together the panko and milk until combined. Set mixture aside to soak for 5 to 10 minutes while you prepare the other ingredients.

Combine remaining ingredients. Add the ground beef, ground pork, garlic, eggs, Parmesan, fresh herbs, onion and Worcestershire sauce to the mixing bowl. Sprinkle the oregano, salt, black pepper and crushed red pepper flakes evenly on top. Use your hands to mix the ingredients until evenly combined, being careful not to overmix.

Form the meatballs. Using a medium cookie scoop or a spoon, scoop and roll the mixture into 2-tablespoon balls and place them on the prepared baking sheet. (I recommend greasing your hands with a bit of olive oil to prevent the mixture from sticking.)
Bake. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer measures the internal temperature of the meatballs to be 160°F. Remove pan and transfer to a wire cooling rack.
Serve. Serve meatballs immediately and enjoy!

title: Conch Fritters: Bahamian Style
description: Traditional Bahamian conch fritters with a zesty dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: red & yellow & green bell pepper, diced

instructions.text: Heat the oil in large pot or deep fryer to 365°F (185°C).
In a bowl, mix the flour, egg and milk.
Season with cayenne pepper, seasoning salt, salt, pepper and red pepper flakes.
Mix in the conch meat, onion, red & yellow & green bell pepper, celery and garlic.
Drop the batter by rounded tablespoons into the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
BE CAREFUL!
Remove the basket or with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Now, is the time to slightly season, again.
In a bowl, mix the ketchup, lime juice, mayonnaise, hot sauce, salt & pepper for dipping sauce.
Serve dipping sauce on the side with the fritters.
Enjoy!

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 7

Remove spices, add lemonade and stir. Keep warm for serving at Setting #2. Makes 24 4-ounce servings.

title: Blue Lemon Fizz
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 7

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 7

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 8

title: Kool-Aid Slush
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 8
description: Frozen slushie made with Kool-Aid and 7-Up.

instructions.text: Mix all the above ingredients together and place in plastic container and freeze. Freeze solidly.

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 8

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 8

instructions.text: Combine cream cheese and marshmallow creme, mixing on medium speed, until well blended.

title: Bread - Cheese Souffle
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 10

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 10

instructions.text: Cook sausage; drain well. Mash fine. Add eggs, cheeses and spices. Put 2 strips from one package of rolls side by side to make rectangle. Seal all seams well.
Put 1/3 mixture on roll. Roll lengthwise and seal ends. Put seam side down on baking sheet. Brush with egg. Repeat with other packages.
Bake 20 minutes at 350 degrees or until light brown.

source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 10

title: Corn Bread Pie
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 12
description: Hearty ground beef casserole with corn bread topping.

instructions.text: Brown the beef and onion in a skillet. Add the soup, water, seasonings, corn and green pepper.
Mix well and allow to simmer for 15 minutes. Grease a casserole dish and fill with mixture about 3/4 full, leaving room for the corn bread topping.
Make the corn bread according to directions, and pour over top of the mixture. Don't be surprised when the topping disappears - it will rise during the baking and form a good layer of corn bread.
Bake at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes.

title: Ham with Corn Bread Stuffing
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 12
description: Glazed ham stuffed with corn bread and mandarin orange stuffing.

instructions.text: Bone ham; leave pocket for stuffing. Prepare and bake corn bread, mix according to package instructions. Cool. Crumble into large bowl. Melt margarine in skillet. Saute celery and onion.
Add to mix. Stir in 3/4 cup orange juice, egg, 1 teaspoon seasoned salt. Sprinkle ham with seasoned salt. Stuff pocket with dressing; cover opening with foil.
Bake at 325 degrees for 2 hours. Score ham, brush with sauce. Combine remaining orange juice, corn syrup and soy sauce.
Reduce oven temperature to 300 degrees, bake for 3 hours and 30 minutes to 4 hours basting frequently. Let stand 10 minutes. Garnish with orange slices.

title: Pizza Muffins
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 14
description: Quick pizza appetizers using English muffins.

instructions.text: Spread muffins with pizza sauce. Top with pepperoni, onion, mushrooms and then cheese.
Bake at 325 degrees for 10-15 minutes. Note: Can take 2 tubes of biscuits and spread them on a greased cookie sheet and top with above ingredients.

title: Chili Con Corn Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 14 - Susan B. Anthony #233
description: Hearty chili topped with cheesy corn bread.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Pour chili into lightly greased 8 inch square baking pan.
Prepare corn bread batter according to package directions, stir in cheese.
Bake 30-35 minutes. Cool 5 minutes. Serves 4-6.

title: Meal in Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 14 - Spring Garden Jolly Juniors Cannon Falls
description: Frozen bread dough stuffed with meat and vegetables.

instructions.text: Brown 1 pound ground beef with onion - drain. Cook and drain 1 (10 ounce) package frozen vegetables.
Divide one loaf of frozen bread dough, which has been thawed, into two parts. Roll each half out on a floured board to form a rectangle.
Brush bread with melted butter - leave edges dry. Top with meat, vegetable and shredded cheese.
Roll into loaf and seal end and bottom. Brush outside with melted butter. Make 3 air vents in top of each loaf.
Bake at 375 degrees about 30 minutes. Slice to serve (as a jelly roll).

title: Beans and Franks Corn Bread Bake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 14
description: Comforting beans and franks topped with corn bread.

instructions.text: Combine beans, franks, green pepper and onion in baking dish.
Top with corn bread batter and bake according to corn bread package directions.

title: Supper on a Bread Slice
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 16
description: Open-faced French bread with seasoned ground beef.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients. Cut 1 loaf French bread in half lengthwise.
Spread meat mixture evenly over top surface of bread, then wrap foil around crust side of each half, leaving top uncovered.
Place on cookie sheet and bake in moderate 325 degree oven for 25 minutes. Garnish with strips of cheese.
Bake 5 minutes longer. To serve, cut slices across or diagonally. (I don't usually use grated cheese, I use strips of cheese and bake 5 minutes longer.)

title: Stuffed Pita Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 16

instructions.text: Prepare fresh vegetables and cheese.

Beat egg and milk and add to bread mix; let stand until absorbed. Bring water to boil (add salt); make large balls and drop into boiling water.
Cook 10 minutes; drain and run cold water on.

title: Bread Bones

title: Broccoli Bread Quiche
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 18
description: Healthy quiche with whole grain bread crust.

ingredients.item: beaten eggs (or equivalent no cholesterol egg substitute)

instructions.text: Toast bread lightly, cut each slice in half. Arrange bread slices in a small non-stick baking pan.
Layer broccoli on top. Stir yogurt into eggs until blended, then spoon over broccoli.
Sprinkle with nutmeg, salt and lemon pepper.
Bake, uncovered, in a preheated oven at 350 degrees for 60 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

title: Mu Shu Pork in Pita Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 20
description: Asian-inspired pork stir-fry served in pita bread.

ingredients.item: pork chops, cut into strips (1 1/2 to 2 inches long)

instructions.text: Mix pork, cornstarch, water, and soy sauce. Cut onions into 2 pieces then into thin strips.
Heat wok or skillet until very hot, pour in 1 tablespoon oil then add eggs. Cook until dry, break cooked eggs up into small pieces. Put on plate.
Reheat wok and pour in remaining oil, add onions then stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the pork and stir-fry until it changes color and separates into strips (if meat sticks, add more oil).
Add cabbage and salt, stir-fry 2 more minutes. Add eggs, stir until all is heated through. In pita bread spread hoisin sauce, then fill.

title: Pocket Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 20
description: Homemade pita/pocket bread.

instructions.text: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Add salt and mix well.
Let rise and shape into pockets. Bake until puffed.

title: Haystack Chocolate Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 34
description: Chocolate pancakes topped with coconut-pecan topping and strawberry fluff.

instructions.text: Prepare coconut-pecan topping. Combine evaporated milk, sugar, egg yolks, butter, vanilla, flaked coconut, and chopped pecans. Cook over medium heat until thickened.
Prepare pancakes with milk, eggs and vegetable oil according to package directions for 2 cups mix. Preheat griddle.
Using scant 1/4 cup batter for each pancake, cook over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes or until underside is browned and surface is bubbly.
Serve with warm Coconut-Pecan topping. Makes 16 to 18 servings.

title: German Oven Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 34
description: Puffy oven-baked pancakes with fruit topping.

instructions.text: Combine and set aside. Heat to very warm, 2 cups milk and 1/4 c. oleo - then add above mixture.
Beat 3 eggs slightly and add; beat until smooth; this can be refrigerated up to 4 days but after 2 days, add 2 more tablespoons sugar, makes 10 to 12.

title: Caramel Ring
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 36
description: Sweet caramel pull-apart bread using Pillsbury biscuits.

instructions.text: Mix and pat together in bottom of large ring mold. 1/3 c. butter, melted, 3/4 c. white sugar.
Mix together sugar and cinnamon. Dip each biscuit in butter, then in sugar mixture, covering the entire biscuit.
Stand on edge in mold. Bake at 375 degrees for 30 minutes. Nuts can be added to first mixture.
Can be made ahead and held in refrigerator for 1/2 day.

title: Overnight Coffee Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 36
description: Make-ahead coffee cake with frozen dough balls.

instructions.text: Combine dry pudding mix with brown sugar and pecans. Place frozen dough balls in well greased bundt pan. Pour melted butter over dough so each ball is coated.
Sprinkle pudding mixture over dough balls. Place in freezer overnight. Remove from freezer and bake at 350 degrees until golden brown for 45 to 50 minutes. Invert on plate and serve.

title: Granola Cereal
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Homemade granola with oats, nuts, and dried fruit.

instructions.text: Combine (except raisins) in a large bowl. Then combine: 1/2 c. (each) honey, oil, water, 1 tsp (each) salt, vanilla.
Add to dry ingredients; mix well. Spread in two 10x15 pans that have been sprayed with Pam. Bake 1 hour at 250 degrees, stirring every 15 minutes.
The last 15 minutes, mix in the raisins evenly and turn off the oven; remove pans and let cool before storing in an airtight container. Serve with milk; no sugar.

title: Waffles
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Basic waffle recipe that can be made ahead.

instructions.text: Combine and set aside. Heat to very warm, 2 cups milk and 1/4 c. oleo - then add above mixture.
Beat 3 eggs slightly and add; beat until smooth; this can be refrigerated up to 4 days but after 2 days, add 2 more tablespoons sugar, makes 10 to 12.

title: Wagon Wheel Sausage Pie - Breakfast
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Hearty breakfast pie with sausage, hash browns, and cream cheese.

instructions.text: Brown sausage and set aside. Prepare hash browns according to package.
Combine ingredients and bake until set.

title: Baked Spanish Potato Omelet
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 42
description: Spanish-style potato omelet baked in the oven.

instructions.text: Beat eggs until fluffy. Fold in remaining ingredients. Spray a round, non-stick cake pan with 25 to 30 minutes until no-fat frying.
Spoon in omelet mixture. Bake at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes until eggs are set. Cut into wedges.
The cooked ham can be replaced with leftover roast poultry, seafood or water packed tuna.

title: Mushroom Quiche
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Rich mushroom quiche with Swiss cheese.

instructions.text: Prepare mushrooms with 2 tablespoons minced scallions. Cook in 3 tablespoons butter. Stir in wine if desired. Mix cream.
Stir in teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Pour mushrooms in the cream and egg mixture.
Pour mixture and eggs together. Pour into partially baked pie shell. Sprinkle with cheese and dot with butter. Bake at 375 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes.

title: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Light and fluffy pancakes made with cottage cheese.

instructions.text: Beat the eggs with fructose and salt. Add cottage cheese, milk and beat until smooth.
Stir in melted butter. Add flour and beat until smooth.
Turn when lightly browned and brown on other side. Serve with hot syrup. Makes 12 pancakes.

title: Roadrunners Rice and Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Quick and easy breakfast with rice, eggs, and cheese.

instructions.text: Cook rice as directed, drain any excess liquid. Put into frying pan and pour beaten eggs over the top of rice.
Begin to scramble egg and add cheese until done. NOTE: Cook rice the night before it makes a real quick easy breakfast. NOTE: Also you can add some turkey ham or chicken.

title: Critter's French Toast
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Crispy French toast with Bran Flakes coating.

instructions.text: Combine eggs, milk, salt and vanilla in shallow dish. Dip bread into mixture, turning well and allowing time for both sides to absorb liquid and place in a single layer on a well greased baking sheet.
Drizzle with butter. Bake in 450 degree oven about 10 minutes or until brown. Serve with warm maple syrup or honey butter. Serves 3.

title: Stuffed Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Deviled eggs with turkey ham.

instructions.text: Cut eggs in half lengthwise, remove yolks, mash. Add remaining ingredients and pack into whites.

title: Fish Omelet
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Protein-rich omelet with halibut or other fish.

instructions.text: Make a cream sauce with first 3 ingredients and seasonings and add fish well mashed.
Beat eggs and mix lightly with fish. Bake in mold, covered with oiled paper over pan of hot water for 1 1/2 hours.

title: Fudd's Blueberry Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Fluffy pancakes with fresh blueberries and honey.

instructions.text: Mix ingredients and cook on griddle. Add blueberries to batter before cooking.

title: Cheese Grits
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 50

instructions.text: Add grits to boiling water. Boil 2-3 minutes. Turn off heat. Add the remaining ingredients. Pour in greased casserole dish. Sprinkle with paprika. Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees. Serves 6.

title: Layered Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 50

instructions.text: Trim the crust from the bread. Toast the bread. With a cookie cutter, cut circles. Line a 9 x 13 inch pan with the bread scraps.
Layer the Monterey Jack, cooked spinach, ham, mushrooms, and the toast circles. Mix eggs, milk, onion, salt and dry mustard. Pour over the circles to soak them.
Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese. Cover. Let stand overnight. Bake at 325 degrees for 55 minutes. Serves 12.

title: Brunch Souffle
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 51

ingredients.item: slices bread, cut into 1/4 inch cubes

instructions.text: Prepare night before. Brown sausage - drain. Spread in 9x13x2 pan. Beat eggs. Blend in milk, mustard, salt, bread cubes and cheese. Pour mixture over sausage. Cover pan and refrigerate overnight.
Uncover and bake at 350 degrees for about one hour.

title: Huevos Rancheros with Green Chili Sauce
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 53

instructions.text: Saute pork until cooked through. Add onion and butter. Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 hour. Thicken with flour and water as needed.
For 8 servings: Heat 2 flour tortillas and top each with 1 egg cooked as desired. Cover with green chili sauce and sprinkle with shredded Cheddar cheese.

title: Brunch Enchiladas
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 53

instructions.text: Combine ham, onions, green pepper. Spoon about 1/3 cup mixture onto each tortilla and roll up.
Place seam side down in greased 11x17 baking dish. Mix eggs, cream, flour, salt, garlic and Tabasco. Pour over tortillas.
Cover and chill overnight. Bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 45-50 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese last 5 minutes.

title: Curried Fruit
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Layer above in order in a 2 quart oblong pan (greased). Bake 45 minutes at 300 degrees.

Heat oven to 325 degrees. Drain fruits well. In small pot, melt butter, add sugar and curry. Place fruits in a 1 1/2 quart casserole. Pour the butter mixture over all. Mix well. Bake 1 hour uncovered. Excellent with ham or lamb. 12 servings.

title: Fruit Mold with Yogurt
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Dissolve Jello in boiling water. Add all fruit and juices. Pour half into large mold and set. Spread with yogurt. Pour remaining Jello mixture over and chill until firm.

title: Cinnamon Coffee Bar
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Mix shortening and sugar. Add egg and coffee. Blend dry ingredients and add to mixture. Spread in greased pan. Bake at 350 degrees. Top with powdered sugar glaze.

title: Benedictine Sandwich
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 59

instructions.text: Grate cucumbers and drain well. Grate onion. Blend these into cream cheese and add enough mayo to make a soft spread. Season lightly and add drops of coloring to make a delicate green. Makes 1 1/2 cups. Great for finger sandwiches or stuffing tomatoes/mushrooms.

title: Seafood Luncheon Dish
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 59

instructions.text: Combine ingredients placing shrimp on top. Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees. Serve with sauce: 1 can cream of mushroom soup plus 1/3 cup milk, heated.

title: Maridadi Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 61

instructions.text: Spread one side of each slice of toast with softened butter. Beat the egg whites with salt until stiff but not dry. Mound the beaten whites on top of the 6 toast slices.

With a spoon, carefully lift one egg yolk and press into the center of the mounded egg whites. Bake in a very hot oven (475 degrees) for 4 to 6 minutes until meringues are lightly browned. Serve immediately. Makes 3 to 6 servings.

title: Crab Breakfast Casserole
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 61

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients. Place in a greased 9 x 9 inch casserole dish and let set in refrigerator overnight.
Remove from refrigerator 1 hour before baking. Bake in a 325 degree oven for 1 hour.

title: Fruit Pizza
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 63

ingredients.item: Pillsbury's Best Sugar Cookie Dough (20 oz)

instructions.text: Freeze dough for one hour. Line a 14 inch pizza pan with foil. Slice dough 1/8 inch thick and line pan, overlap slices but don't flatten into pan.
Bake at 375 degrees for 12 minutes or until browned. Cool completely. Invert crust onto another pan, remove foil, put it back on the same pizza pan.
Combine cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla until blended. Spread on crust, arrange fruit. Put preserves and water in bowl and stir to glaze-like consistency. Pour over fruit; chill.

title: Lemony Poppy Seed Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 63

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Using solid shortening, grease and flour bottom only of 9"x5" loaf pan.
In large bowl, blend all ingredients at low speed until moistened. Beat 2 minutes at medium speed. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake at 325 degrees for 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes; remove from pan. Wrap tightly and store in refrigerator. Yield: 1 loaf.

title: Skillet Orange Coffee Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 67

ingredients.item: Pillsbury's best all purpose or unbleached flour

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Grease 10" oven proof skillet. Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup, level off.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. In small bowl, combine orange juice, oil and eggs; add to dry ingredients, mixing well.
Pour batter into prepared skillet. In small bowl, combine bread crumbs, sugar, cinnamon, margarine and orange peel with fork until crumbly. Sprinkle topping evenly over batter.
Bake at 350 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes; serve warm. 12 servings.

title: Mini Cheesecakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 68

instructions.text: Line muffin tin with foil cupcake liners. Place 1 vanilla wafer in each liner. Mix cream cheese, vanilla and sugar on medium speed until well blended. Add eggs and mix well.

Pour over wafers, filling each one almost full. Bake 25 minutes at 325 degrees. Remove from muffin pan when cool. Chill. Top with fruit, preserves, nuts or chocolate. These are quick and easy and can be cooled quickly in freezer.

title: Peanut Butter Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 68

instructions.text: Prepare pans. Cream shortening. Add slowly and beat in 1 cup brown sugar and peanut butter. In another bowl, beat together 2 eggs and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Add this to the first mixture and beat well.

Sift together flour, salt and powder. Add dry ingredients alternately to first mixture with 1 cup milk with vanilla. Pour mixture into pans and bake at once until firm in center. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.

title: Mexican Fruit Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 72

instructions.text: Hand mix only. Bake one hour and 10 minutes. Comes out very moist. Makes a big cake. Very good.

CAKE: Mix all ingredients in large mixing bowl. Stir by hand until completely mixed. Pour into greased and floured 13 x 9 inch baking pan or dish. Bake 40 to 45 minutes in metal pan, 30 to 35 minutes in glass baking dish. ICING: Mix together. Ice when cake is cool.

title: Mountain Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 72

instructions.text: Separate eggs and reserve whites in small bowl. Beat egg yolks, add sugar gradually and beat. Add bread crumbs, nuts, farina, and baking powder one at a time, beating after each addition.
Beat egg white stiff and fold into mixture. Bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes. When cool, crumble into several pieces. Before serving, fold cake into whipped cream.

Pile into mountain form and garnish with cherries. This can also be put in a child's sand pain and sprinkled with crushed Oreo cookies. Garnish with a plastic flower and use sand shovel as serving spoon.

title: Earthquake Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 74

instructions.text: Combine the 1 cup of pecans and 1 cup of coconut and put in the bottom of a 9 x 13 inch baking pan.

Mix the German chocolate cake as directed on the box. Pour over the nuts and coconut. Over low heat, melt the margarine and cream cheese. Slowly stir in the entire box of confectioners sugar. Spoon cream cheese mixture over cake mix. Do not spread, just drop over top.
Bake cake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.

title: Toll House Cup Cakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 74

instructions.text: Prepare graham cracker crust (20 graham crackers, 4 tablespoons sugar and 1/4 pound melted butter) and press into springform pan. Cream 1 pound of cream cheese, 2 eggs and 1 cup sugar. Pour mixture into crust and bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees. Cool 20 minutes.

Make top dressing using 1 pint sour cream, 4 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Pour mixture over cooled cake and return to oven for 5 minutes at 500 degrees. After cake cools, refrigerate several hours before serving.
